messages:
Priya Patel: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands on process topics (release cadence, oncall, quality bars, SLAs). Drop short Qs here and we'll answer in the live Q&A shortly.

Alex Chen: Are weekly release trains still our goal for hosted API? noticed a few slips.

Priya Patel: Yes, weekly is the goal. Slips happened due to infra migrations and emergency rollbacks. We'll publish an exceptions policy.

Samir Gupta: Canary window + rollback criteria? and do runtime PRs need the full perf suite before merge?

Priya Patel: Canary: 30m default. Rollback if error-rate >0.5% above baseline or p95 latency +15% sustained 5m. Runtime-impacting PRs need smoke perf checks pre-merge; full perf suite runs post-merge and can block promotions. Use the "perf-test" PR label for special runners.

Marta Lf3pez: Oncall: any move to 2-week rotations? 1-week is rough for some teams.

Priya Patel: We'll pilot 2-week infra rotations next quarter. Runtime stays 1-week for now. Typical coverage: runtime 1 primary + 1 secondary; infra 1 primary + 2 secondaries. Rota + shadowing doc coming.

Alex Chen: Will Releases UI show route-level canary health?

Priya Patel: Yes  route-level p50/p95/error-rate and a canary health badge. @Alex Chen please mock and link in the follow-up doc.

Samir Gupta: SLA tiers? hosted still 99.9? Dedicated higher SLA options?

Priya Patel: Hosted public SLA stays 99.9. Dedicated customers can opt into 99.95 with reserved capacity + contract. We'll publish an SLA matrix next week.

Priya Patel: Action items: I'll draft the FAQ + one-pager. @Marta Lf3pez to write hosted vs dedicated release differences. @Alex Chen to mock console. Post PRs to #eng-docs and we'll iterate.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for train/2026-03-15 (build 2026.03.15-b3c2).

Marta Lf3pez: I'll open the draft PR by EOD tomorrow.

Alex Chen: Linking Figma mock once uploaded.
